question: The last ruler of the Mauryan Empire was:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Brihadratha**____** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Brihadratha Maurya** was the last ruler of the Mauryan Empire, ruling from 187–185 BCE: 
 
• Brihadratha **was assassinated by his general, Pushyamitra Shunga, who then established the Shunga Empire. **
 
• **Some other rulers of the Mauryan Empire include: **
 
 
• **Chandragupta: Ruled from 320–298 BCE**
 
• **Bindusara: Ruled from 298–272 BCE**
 
• **Ashoka: Ruled from 268–232 BCE**
 
• **Dasharatha: Ruled from 232–224 BCE**
 
• **Samprati: Ruled from 224–215 BCE**
 
• **Shalishuka: Ruled from 215–202 BCE**
 
• **Devavarman: Ruled from 202–195 BCE**
 
• **Shatadhanva: Ruled from 195–187 BCE**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dasharatha Maurya**

 
 
• Dynasty: Maurya Dynasty
 
• Significance: Dasharatha Maurya was one of the ancient rulers of the Maurya dynasty, often noted for his reign before the rise of Emperor Ashoka. Not much is known about his reign, as historical records are sparse, but he is believed to have contributed to the consolidation of Mauryan rule in early periods.
 
 
 
• **Shalishuka**
 
 
• Dynasty: Maurya Dynasty
 
• Significance: Shalishuka was a king of the Maurya dynasty, who ruled after Ashoka's reign. He is most notable for being one of the successors during a period of relative instability within the Maurya Empire. His rule is not as well-documented as that of Ashoka, but he played a part in maintaining the empire's control in its later years.
 
 
 
• **Samprati**
 
 
• Dynasty: Maurya Dynasty
 
• Significance: **Samprati was a Mauryan emperor, considered to be a follower of Jainism.** After the reign of Ashoka, Samprati continued the promotion of Jainism and is credited with spreading Jain philosophy and establishing Jain centers across the empire. His reign marked a continuation of the influence of Jainism in the Maurya Empire following Ashoka's policies.
